The Fastest Way To Develop An Unpassable.overview: John Danaher's no-gi guard retention course, eight volumes. Volume 1 covers twelve essential body movements for retention. Volume 2 covers how opponents pass (the five steps of guard passing, the three danger zones). Volume 3 covers retention against distance passing (high leg and inside leg methods). Volume 4 covers countering head control (elbow post, inside position leg scissor). Volume 5 covers retention against hips-centred passing (negating body locks, three safety positions). Volume 6 covers defending against double scoop grips (locked and unlocked hands). Volume 7 covers retention against head and shoulder control and stopping half guard passes. Volume 8 covers sit-out half guard variations against crossface and reverse crossface.
The Fastest Way To Develop An Unpassable.for: No-gi guard players who get passed.
key: Danger zones and steps of passing
Retention vs body locks and scoop grips

The Top Game Toolkit by Owen Livesey.overview: Owen Livesey's top game course, three parts (about 1.5 hours). Part 1 covers the hand fight and slide-by passes. Part 2 covers passing seated guard (toreando, the upside-down C grip). Part 3 covers passing open guard (double under pass, stack pass).
The Top Game Toolkit by Owen Livesey.for: Gi and no-gi passers wanting a compact passing toolkit.

Tommy Langaker & Espen Mathiesen - Vikin.overview: Norwegian competitors Tommy Langaker and Espen Mathiesen's 'Viking' passing, four parts. Part 1 covers knee slide passing and getting to a reverse De La Riva passing position. Part 2 covers the 'Viking knee smash', the hip switch pass and the hip switch to back take. Part 3 covers 'Loki's trap' (a stack pass against reverse De La Riva) into the 'Viking power lift' pass, and over-under concepts. Part 4 covers over-under to stack pass variations and to the leg drag.
Tommy Langaker & Espen Mathiesen - Vikin.for: Gi and no-gi passers facing reverse De La Riva and modern open guards.
key: Over-under to stack and leg drag
